_note: Thomas, 2026-09-06: 'ready to check out the rest of the uk/GB/ireland/scotland and Au' — round 2 of the thin-coverage direction, and the Australian half of it. AU had 24 nodes, almost all of them local-government rates, valuation Acts and grants-commission machinery: an OECD economy with no CPI, no national accounts, no labour force survey, no balance of payments, no central bank publication and no statistical law in the graph. This round mints the national core and the statutory spine (Census and Statistics Act 1905), and wires four nodes that were already present — the Census, the Estimated Resident Population and Government Finance Statistics — into it. Every url and every evidence_url was raw-verified HTTP 200 before use and every quote read live from the cited URL in the cloud sandbox. One exception, recorded on the edges concerned: rba.gov.au serves a JavaScript shell to a text fetcher ('It appears JavaScript is currently blocked'), so the Statement on Monetary Policy quotes were read from the RBA's own August 2026 PDF on the same host.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index, Australia
reports.description: Australia's quarterly consumer price index, measuring price change for a basket of goods and services representative of those acquired by metropolitan private households. The 17th series comprises 87 expenditure classes, each with its own weight; weights have been updated annually since the December quarter 2017. The headline measure is the All groups CPI for the weighted average of the eight capital cities, published alongside the trimmed mean and weighted median underlying series.

reports.title: Australian System of National Accounts
reports.description: Australia's annual national accounts: national income, expenditure and product, plus input-output tables, state estimates, capital stock, financial accounts, balance sheets, reconciliation accounts and productivity estimates. The 2008-09 issue was the first compiled on a 2008 SNA basis. ABS's application of the standard is set out in Australian System of National Accounts: Concepts, Sources and Methods.

reports.title: Labour Force, Australia
reports.description: Australia's monthly labour force release — employment, unemployment, participation and hours worked — drawn from the Labour Force Survey, a monthly sample survey of households. Its conceptual framework follows the resolutions of the International Conferences of Labour Statisticians, and its estimates are calculated so that they add to independent population benchmarks based on the quarterly Estimated Resident Population.

reports.title: Household Expenditure Survey, Australia
reports.description: Australia's household budget survey: a periodic survey of the expenditures of different household types in each of the capital cities, currently run six-yearly. ABS's own CPI methodology names it as the authoritative source the CPI basket is based on, and as the source used to re-weight the CPI in the years it is available.
reports.cadence_note: Six-yearly. ABS's CPI methodology: the HES 'is used to re-weight the CPI in the years where it is available, currently six-yearly'.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, Australia
reports.description: Australia's quarterly international accounts: the current, capital and financial accounts of the balance of payments and the international investment position, including net foreign equity and net foreign debt. Compiled on the IMF's BPM6 framework alongside the 2008 SNA, from data collected by the ABS under the Census and Statistics Act 1905 together with export and import declarations collected by the Department of Home Affairs.

reports.title: Statement on Monetary Policy
reports.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly account of economic conditions and the outlook, carrying the Bank's published forecasts for output, the labour market, wages and inflation against the 2-3 per cent inflation target. Its forecast tables and charts are sourced to the ABS among others, and its labour market series are constructed from ABS Labour Force Survey outputs.

reports.title: Census and Statistics Act 1905
reports.description: The Act relating to the census and statistics of the Commonwealth. It gives the Australian Statistician the authority to conduct statistical collections, including the Census of Population and Housing; section 8 requires the Census to be taken every fifth year; section 9(2) requires the Statistician to collect the information necessary to compile quarterly statistics of the population of each State. It also carries the confidentiality obligation ABS releases cite when they state that results have been confidentialised.

dependencies.basis: RESEARCHED 2026-09-06 (AU national core round). dependencies.basis: RESEARCHED 2026-09-06 (AU national core round). The Statement's published forecast table carries a Consumer Price Index row, and the table's own source line names the ABS; the memo items are deflated by the Consumer Price Index. Graded B deliberately, not A, on the same reasoning as gb-boe-mpr -> gb-ons-cpi: the artefact is named in a table row and footnote rather than in a sourcing sentence, and the source line names the agency, not the release (PLAYBOOK-CORPUS section 7, 'naming the agency is not naming the artefact'). Read live as the August 2026 PDF from rba.gov.au (HTTP 200); the HTML landing page is a JavaScript shell to a text fetcher.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Real Wage Price Index and non-farm average earnings per hour worked are both deflated by Consumer Price Index.

_dropped.why: NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The Labour Force methodology (read live, HTTP 200) says 'The conceptual framework used in Australia's Labour Force Survey aligns closely with the standards and guidelines set out in Resolutions of International Conferences of Labour Statisticians.' That names the conference series generically, in the plural, and no specific resolution — the same shape that stopped gb-ons-lfs -> icls-work-statistics-resolution on 2026-09-06 (PLAYBOOK-CORPUS section 7, 'naming the agency is not naming the artefact'). The page's historical-changes list names ICLS 1954, ICLS 1961 and ICLS/ICSE 1993, none of which is the resolution concerning statistics of work, employment and labour underutilization. Decided the same way as the UK for the same reason; both are almost certainly real and both want the document that names the resolution.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The ABS CPI methodology, read in full, never names COICOP. Its 87 expenditure classes are an ABS classification, not a COICOP mapping, and the only international-classification sentence on the page concerns the 17th International Conference of Labour Statisticians' resolution on an index excluding housing and financial services — a different artefact from the CPI's classification basis and not a dependency of the CPI on it.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. abs.gov.au's /census/* pages are JavaScript shells to a text fetcher (about 1-4KB of nav markup and no body), so no ABS census methodology text was read this round. The Legislative framework page, which does fetch, names the Act and not any UN recommendation. Not a claim about the site: it is a claim about the fetcher, and the pages are open in a real browser.
